source.title: Control Allocation in Neural Network Optimization: Joint Affine Control of Weight and Bias Updates
source.authors: Gong-Yue Zhang; Yi-Xuan Sheng; Zhi-Yong Wang; Dong-Han Liu; Wei-Hong Ren; Hong-Hai Liu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The reference list identifies arXiv:2608.02991 as the antecedent study [13], although this record is for the supplied paper titled “Control Allocation in Neural Network Optimization: Joint Affine Control of Weight and Bias Updates.”
record.tranche_reason: The study reports optimizer and control comparisons with test metrics, and finds a bounded useful regime plus underfitting under excessive affine control. Its own discussion says those results do not establish a task-independent performance ordering.
record.gate_note: The optimizer and control comparisons report outcomes on the study’s controlled benchmark and transfer suite. Same-state allocation checks and test-performance values used only as diagnostics are not evidence for the version-specific effects unless they measure the version’s named outcome.
record.test_reason: The study tests update-allocation controls, not any listed claim version. Its synthetic partial-adaptivity sweep does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on image or language benchmarks. Its language-task comparisons use AdamW, Muon and affine variants, without an SGD comparator. Wilson et al. is discussed as background; neither these comparisons nor control-induced underfitting tests V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Frozen-state replay verifies exact allocation-control laws. Moderate controls improve selected metrics on the five-seed synthetic benchmark, excessive affine control causes underfitting, and the single-seed transfer suite provides descriptive evidence only. The authors do not establish a task-independent performance ordering.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates coordinate and affine allocation controls, same-state replay, and trajectory-level outcomes; it does not reproduce the natural-label memorization/generalization experiments or the named optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Control strength changes outcomes: coordinate control has an intermediate optimum, and high affine exponents produce underfitting. Transfer rankings vary across datasets; only seed 42 is available.

fits_no_version.finding: On the five-seed synthetic benchmark, coordinate control raises test accuracy from 89.54% to 92.09%; joint affine control reaches 92.57% at exponent 1 but falls to 64.09% at exponent 2 with underfitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Allocation controls have a bounded useful range on this synthetic distribution-shift task; excessive affine control impairs training.

fits_no_version.finding: Across four seed-42 language tasks, joint affine exponent 1 has the best average rank, 1.50; exponent 2 ranks last on both language-modeling tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Moderate affine control performs competitively in this single-seed suite, with dataset-dependent outcomes.

record.problems: The controlled benchmark has five seeds; the transfer suite has one seed and is explicitly descriptive. The controlled task includes a test-time distribution shift. The authors state the common protocol does not replace a fully tuned optimizer comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The transfer table’s per-dataset raw accuracy and perplexity values were not extracted separately; the study reports aggregate within-dataset ranks and average rank in the rank table, used here to keep the transfer comparison compact.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization versus natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD or momentum-SGD held-out performance on image/language benchmarks, tuning dependence, switching optimizers, and recovery through decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons with norm/margin measures.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Delete the V4 limits_scope verdict: varying control outcomes and limited replication do not qualify a claim whose named optimizer comparison was not tested. The supplied header identifies this as arXiv:2608.02991v2, while reference [13] assigns that identifier to a differently titled antecedent; this internal source-identity inconsistency remains unresolved. Assessment uses only the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test memorization of random labels alongside generalization on natural labels.
Does not vary network width or test generalization beyond an interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected architectures.

Does not compare Adam with SGD or momentum SGD under the version’s tuning protocol; the controlled benchmark is synthetic and has a test-time distribution shift. Transfer results use one seed. The authors state their protocol does not replace a fully tuned optimizer comparison.
Does not vary batch size or test large-batch training.
Does not test dropout or the joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- or margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized examples or retrain after example removal.
